importance_ranking.reason: Buyers (government health departments, hospital chains, EPC contractors) scan images first to identify the structural type, scale, and finish quality of the facility — a modular ICU block, a multi-storey turnkey hospital, and a portable field hospital are visually distinct and non-interchangeable. Absence of a credible exterior/interior image signals an unserious or incomplete listing and causes immediate skip in a high-value procurement context.

Hospital type, bed capacity, number of floors, wall panel type, and included facilities (OT, ICU, OPD) are primary shortlisting criteria — buyers cannot evaluate fit without these. A listing without specs cannot be compared against tender requirements or project scope.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised specialists — Pressmach, EPACK Prefab, Wedge India, KEF-TAHPI — carry brand weight through NABH compliance track record, government project credentials, and post-sale service capability; buyers actively shortlist by manufacturer reputation in this high-stakes, high-value category.
importance_ranking.reason: Prefabricated hospital procurement is a high-value, compliance-critical decision — buyers must verify NABH alignment, NBC structural compliance, government project track record, and post-installation service capability before engaging. An unknown supplier with matching specs is still a procurement risk; company identity is a primary trust gate.

Every prefabricated hospital is custom-engineered and project-quoted; no meaningful per-unit list price exists. Buyers use any indicative price only as a budget sanity check after spec and company qualification — final price is always negotiated through a formal tender or RFQ process.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Modular ward/ICU add-ons may be quoted per sq ft; portable single units quoted per unit — but these sub-segments do not create buyer confusion because the quoting basis is established during project scoping, not from a listing card.
importance_ranking.reason: Project-based pricing means there is no per-unit price on the listing to confuse or misread. Unit ambiguity cannot arise when every sale is scope-quoted.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the facility IS — a General Hospital, Primary Health Centre, Field Hospital, or Diagnostic Centre are non-interchangeable project types with entirely different scope, regulatory requirements, and price points, making this the primary product-class separator.

PUF, Rockwool, EPS, and Glasswool panels represent distinct thermal, fire, and acoustic performance tiers with significant price deltas — a buyer specifying Rockwool (fire-rated) for an OT cannot substitute EPS, making this the primary technical grade separator within any hospital type.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Bed count is the primary sizing parameter for hospital procurement — government tenders and private hospital projects are scoped and budgeted by bed capacity (25-bed PHC vs 100-bed district hospital), and sellers need this to determine project scale and price.

NABH accreditation alignment is a prerequisite for government empanelment and insurance cashless services — buyers from state health departments and private hospital chains require this confirmation before shortlisting a supplier.

Total built-up area (sq ft) is the primary project sizing metric used alongside bed capacity — buyers and EPC contractors need this to assess scope, compare proposals, and validate against site constraints.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Bed count is the single most important sizing signal — it determines project scale, structural scope, MEP requirements, and price tier, enabling sellers to immediately assess fit and provide an accurate indicative quote.

Number of floors determines structural engineering complexity, foundation requirements, and regulatory compliance pathway — a G+2 hospital requires fundamentally different design and cost inputs than a single-storey facility, and sellers need this to scope the project accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The type of facility (General Hospital, PHC, Field Hospital, Diagnostic Centre, COVID Hospital) defines the entire functional brief — sellers need this to determine which room configurations, MEP systems, and compliance standards apply before they can respond meaningfully.
